actions.name: Review urine microalbumin/creatinine ratio
actions.result: Urine albumin/creatinine ratio 18 mg/g (within normal <30 mg/g).

actions.name: Review dilated retinal screening status

actions.name: Guide camera inspection of infusion-site/pump sites
actions.result: Patient shows abdomen on camera: infusion sites rotated appropriately, no lipohypertrophy, erythema, or signs of infection.

actions.name: Guide camera inspection of feet

actions.name: Review pump/CGM alert settings
actions.result: Low alert threshold set at 70 mg/dL, high alert at 250 mg/dL. Settings have not been modified in over a year despite the current glycemic pattern.

actions.result: Diabetes Distress Scale score elevated (screen-positive for diabetes-related burnout); PHQ-2 score 1/6 (screen-negative for major depression). Patient denies suicidal ideation.

actions.name: Administer AUDIT-C alcohol screening questionnaire
actions.result: AUDIT-C score 7/12 (positive screen for risky drinking pattern; threshold for further assessment in men is ≥4). Patient confirms weekend drinking after shifts; denies morning drinking or withdrawal symptoms.

actions.name: Review current diabetes medication/supply list
actions.result: Insulin pump (rapid-acting insulin aspart reservoir), CGM sensor, no other glucose-lowering agents; no GLP-1 or metformin currently prescribed.

actions.name: Review home blood pressure/weight trend over past year
actions.result: Weight stable 69-71 kg over past year; BP consistently 110-120/70-78 mmHg on home cuff readings.

artifacts.body: 23 y/o male with T1DM since age 9 on pump/CGM therapy, A1c 8.5% (up from 7.6%). Discussed carb counting review and importance of consistent bolusing. Patient reports he is 'doing his best' with school and work schedule. Deferred retinal exam referral pending patient scheduling; patient states he will arrange through university health clinic. No DKA episodes reported. Plan: continue current pump settings, recheck A1c and CGM download in 6 months, strong encouragement to complete overdue dilated eye exam and resume regular meal bolusing.

objectives.text: Interpret CGM ambulatory glucose profile and pump bolus history together to identify discordance between reported and actual bolusing frequency.

Elicit, with empathy, the behavioral drivers of glycemic pattern: fear of hypoglycemia at work, alarm silencing, and weekend binge drinking without food, moving beyond screening-tool scores to the underlying narrative once rapport is established.

Screen for and recognize diabetes burnout/distress as a contributor to nonadherence, distinguishing it from major depression with suicidal ideation, and follow up screen-positive results with direct, empathetic questions to uncover the full picture.
Identify overdue diabetic complication screening (retinal exam) and address nephropathy and lipid risk based on labs.
Recognize the mismatch between the patient's self-report of consistent mealtime bolusing and the objective pump data, and address it nonjudgmentally.

Formulate a management plan within endocrinology scope: adjust pump/CGM settings and alarm strategy, address hypoglycemia risk from alcohol, counsel on carb counting, and refer appropriately for eye care and behavioral health rather than manage those directly.

mismatches.patientClaim: I bolus every time I eat, pretty much like clockwork.
mismatches.recordEvidence: Pump bolus history shows an average of only 2 boluses per day against an estimated 4-5 meals/snacks, with 9 of 14 days having zero boluses after 3pm.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Objective device data often reveals adherence gaps that patients may not fully recognize or may minimize; approach discrepancies with curiosity rather than confrontation to preserve trust and uncover root causes (fear of hypoglycemia, work constraints).

mismatches.patientClaim: I keep meaning to get that eye exam done, I just haven't gotten around to it.
mismatches.recordEvidence: Prior visit note from 6 months ago documents the same unresolved referral for dilated eye exam, deferred pending patient scheduling, with no completion in over 3 years.
mismatches.teachingPoint: Recurring deferred referrals for complication screening need active care coordination (e.g., direct scheduling assistance, reminder systems) rather than repeated verbal encouragement alone.

answerKey.primaryProblem: Suboptimal type 1 diabetes control (HbA1c 9.4%, time in range 38%) driven by behavioral nonadherence: fear-driven bolus omission during bartending shifts, CGM/pump alarm silencing, and weekend binge drinking without food leading to a mixed pattern of daytime hyperglycemia and recurrent nocturnal hypoglycemia, in the context of diabetes burnout.
differential: Nonadherence/behavioral causes of hyperglycemia (fear of hypoglycemia, work-related bolus omission) - supported by pump data
Alcohol-associated nocturnal hypoglycemia (binge drinking without food after shifts) - supported by CGM pattern on Fri/Sat nights
Diabetes distress/burnout contributing to self-care disengagement - supported by screening responses
Insufficient pump basal/bolus settings for current lifestyle (less likely as primary driver given bolus omission is the dominant pattern, but settings review still warranted)
Comorbid thyroid dysfunction contributing to glycemic variability - excluded, TSH normal
Early diabetic nephropathy as explanation for malaise - excluded, albumin/creatinine ratio normal
keyFindings: HbA1c rising trend 7.6% to 8.5% to 9.4% over 12 months
CGM time in range only 38%, with time <54 mg/dL 3% concentrated on Friday/Saturday overnights and marked afternoon/evening hyperglycemia
Pump bolus history shows ~2 boluses/day versus reported 4-5 meals, with 9/14 days lacking any bolus after 3pm
Patient reports fear of hypoglycemia while bartending leads to deliberate bolus omission and alarm silencing
Weekend binge drinking (5-6+ drinks) after shifts, often without eating, temporally matches nocturnal hypoglycemia pattern
Diabetes burnout after 14 years, decreased motivation for self-care, without suicidal ideation
No dilated retinal exam in 3+ years despite prior documented referral
Mildly elevated LDL (118 mg/dL) and triglycerides (190 mg/dL), mildly elevated AST/ALT (may reflect alcohol use), normal renal function and urine albumin/creatinine ratio, normal TSH
plan: Review CGM and pump data collaboratively with patient to show objective bolusing pattern without judgment; explore the gap between intention and behavior

Problem-solve work-shift hypoglycemia fear: consider adjusting correction factors, raising low-glucose suspend threshold, or using temporary basal/activity settings during shifts; discuss using CGM predictive low alerts rather than muting them

Counsel specifically on alcohol-related delayed hypoglycemia risk: avoid drinking without food, consider reducing basal insulin or using a bedtime snack with carbohydrate+protein on drinking nights, ensure glucagon access and that friends/coworkers know how to recognize/treat severe lows

Address diabetes burnout: validate emotional burden, discuss manageable incremental goals, refer to behavioral health/diabetes psychology or certified diabetes care and education specialist for ongoing support
Place/confirm referral for dilated retinal eye exam with active scheduling assistance (not just verbal encouragement) given 3+ year gap
Address modestly elevated LDL and triglycerides with reinforced nutrition counseling and recheck lipid panel in 3-6 months; monitor AST/ALT trend given alcohol use and recheck after counseling
Continue monitoring renal function and urine albumin/creatinine ratio annually (currently normal)
Arrange closer follow-up interval (e.g., 4-6 weeks) with CGM/pump data review to assess response to behavioral and settings changes before next A1c check
redFlags: Recurrent nocturnal glucose <54 mg/dL, especially unwitnessed and alcohol-associated, carries risk for severe hypoglycemia and impaired awareness - requires urgent attention
Diabetes burnout with reduced self-care engagement should be screened for escalation to depression or suicidal ideation at each visit
Overdue diabetic eye screening in setting of 14-year disease duration and poor control raises retinopathy risk and needs timely completion
educationPoints: Pump/CGM download data provide objective adherence information that should be reviewed collaboratively, not as a 'gotcha,' to understand root causes of gaps between stated and actual behavior

Alcohol can cause delayed hypoglycemia for many hours after drinking, especially when combined with insulin on board and inadequate food intake; patient education should include practical harm-reduction strategies rather than abstinence-only messaging if the patient is not ready to stop drinking

Fear of hypoglycemia is a common and legitimate driver of insulin omission, particularly in jobs with safety or social stakes (e.g., service industry); addressing the fear directly (through alarm/threshold adjustments, low-treatment planning) is often more effective than simply repeating adherence instructions

Diabetes burnout is distinct from major depressive disorder but still warrants screening for mood symptoms and suicidal ideation, and benefits from referral to behavioral health or diabetes education support

Routine complication screening (retinal exam, urine albumin/creatinine ratio, lipids) should be actively tracked and re-ordered/rescheduled when overdue, rather than relying solely on patient follow-through

patient.name: Diego Morales
patient.appearance: A young man with short dark hair and an easy smile, wearing a university hoodie, seated in what looks like a small bedroom with a desk and string lights visible behind him. He gestures animatedly and often laughs or jokes before answering more serious questions, though his eyes look tired.

persona.personality: Charming, quick-witted, uses humor to deflect from uncomfortable topics, generally likeable and sociable.
persona.communicationStyle: Casual, conversational, peppers answers with jokes; opens up more when the clinician responds with warmth rather than correction.
persona.emotionalState: Outwardly upbeat but underlying fatigue and discouragement surface when burnout topic is explored; mild embarrassment about drinking and bolus omission.
persona.background: Grew up in Miami after his family emigrated from Colombia when he was young; diagnosed with type 1 diabetes at age 9. Now in his final year of university, juggling a demanding course load with bartending shifts several nights a week to help cover rent and tuition. His mother still lives in Colombia and checks in by phone, but he manages most day-to-day life, including his diabetes care, independently.
speechExamples: Oh man, don't remind me about the eye doctor, I know, I know.
Honestly between work and school I'm just trying to keep my head above water.
I mean, I bolus... most of the time? Okay, let's be real, not always.
Hey, at least my CGM graph looks like a rollercoaster, keeps things exciting.
Yeah, weekends after shifts we usually have a few drinks, nothing crazy... I think.
concerns: Worried the rising A1c means he's 'failing' at managing his diabetes
Anxious about going low while working behind the bar in front of customers
Unsure how to balance diabetes care with school and work demands
Slightly embarrassed to admit how much he's been skipping boluses and drinking

profile.summary: A 23-year-old with 14-year history of type 1 diabetes on pump/CGM therapy presents for follow-up with HbA1c risen from 7.6% to 9.4% over one year. The case teaches reconciling patient self-report with objective CGM/pump data, uncovering fear-driven insulin omission and alcohol-related nocturnal hypoglycemia, screening for diabetes burnout, and coordinating overdue complication screening, all while modeling empathetic, nonjudgmental communication with a charming but avoidant young adult patient.
profile.title: Rising HbA1c in a 23-year-old bartender with type 1 diabetes: unmasking fear-driven insulin omission and alcohol-related nocturnal hypoglycemia
